pr_title: Collect template variable providers from toolchain targets.
pr_body:
They can then be used by rules directly.

Note: genrule does not support per-target toolchains and so this is not
compatible with genrule.

Fixes #5223.

Change-Id: Idf673284a6c91d506e7ed48106050eb10b69f1b6
pr_comments:
> This continues the theme of pushing make variables into explicitly declared dependencies (toolchains) instead of magical places in the configuration, right? i.e. this is in line with the make variable refactorings @lberki has been doing?

Yes, exactly. This allows toolchain authors to directly add new make variables that can be expanded, in targets that are using the provided toolchains.

> is this compatible with @serynth's trimming plans?

Yes, it shouldn't have any impact, as it's not changing anything in the configuration directly.

> Does this specific change add any new power or is it just a preparatory change for genrule integration? If accessing these variables directly through Skylark-defined rules, that power already exists through other (non-template) providers exposed by the toolchain, right?

This is something that current toolchain-like rules, such as cc_toolchain and java_toolchain, do already. This change just allows the already-supplied make variables from those targets to be carried forward by the toolchain resolution system.

Rules can currently provide make variables (via TemplateVariableInfo providers) to direct dependencies.

issue_context.title: Support custom make variables
issue_context.body:
### Description of the feature request:

Say I define a script that has a runtime dependency on the Java compiler. I would write a rule similar to this:

```python
sh_binary(
  name = "foo",
  srcs = ["""
  ...
  $(JAVA) ...
  ...
  """],
)
```

Now, imagine I want to write a similar script that wants to call a binary in the Go, Rust or Haskell toolchains. How do i write such as `sh_binary` rule? Ideally, I'd use a make variable substitution for the compiler, just like for Java.

### Feature requests: what underlying problem are you trying to solve with this feature?

The problem is that there is no easy way to get at the path of a toolchain binary from within an `sh_binary` or `genrule` definition. In general compilers are part of toolchains, so I can't just add a `deps = ["//path/to/compiler"]` to the `sh_binary` rule above and use runfile lookup, because the label for say the compiler in the toolchain is unknown before toolchain resolution. So I wouldn't know what to put in `deps` nor by what name I should do a lookup in the runfiles.

### What's the output of `bazel info release`?

v0.13.0

###  Have you found anything relevant by searching the web?

None found in GitHub issue tracker.
comments:
This is an interesting idea. One option we can look into is allowing toolchain providers to also provide make variables (so you could declare a toolchain type on the genrule and have that work). Something similar is actually being added for C++ currently, but we hadn't envisioned adding similar functionality in general yet.

The other option would be to write your own custom rule that requires the Go toolchain, and use that to generate actions. It's not as simple as a genrule, but it would actually be more portable across different platforms.

I'm going to add this to the toolchains category but I'm not sure it's a feature we'll be able to add soon. Would writing your own rule handle your use case?

What I ended up doing is storing in the toolchain provider a reference to a directory containing symlinks to all the tools I'm interested in, then writing a rule that sets the `PATH` to include that directory. As you say, it's a more complicated route.
Thanks for the update. I'll comment back here if we end up doing anything related to this for Skylark rules.

Work on this is happening, I have a plan to allow toolchains to expose a [TemplateVariableInfo](https://docs.bazel.build/versions/master/skylark/lib/platform_common.html#TemplateVariableInfo) provider, and have that get picked up and exposed in the rule context for variable expansion. Expect some work in a few weeks (there are other changes blocking the way, first).

The new `TemplateVariableInfo` stuff looks very promising, but how do I use it for the use case exposed in the original description of this ticket? To recap, what I want is the following:

```
sh_binary(
  name = "bar",
  srcs = ["bar.sh"],
  args = ["$(FOO)"],
  toolchains = ["//path/to:foo_toolchain_type"],
)
```

To make this work, I would need `$(FOO)` to return the absolute path to the Foo compiler. How do I do this, e.g. if the Foo compiler is actually some `cc_binary` built with Bazel?

To answer your question: you need to define a rule that can define the FOO Make variable, possibly like this:

```
def _impl(ctx):
    path = ctx.attr.path
    return [platform_common.TemplateVariableInfo({'FOO': path})]

foo_supplier = rule(
    implementation = _impl,
    attrs = {
        'path': attr.string(),
    })
```

Then you can do this:
```
foo_supplier(
    name = 'my_foo',
    path = '/path/to/foo')

sh_binary(
    name = 'bar',
    srcs = ['bar.sh'],
    args = ["$(FOO)"],
    toolchains = [':my_foo'],
)
```

You can change the implementation of foo_supplier to take a label and export the path, to take a list of labels and compute a path string somehow, etc etc.

However, if all you really want is to know where a cc_binary is, I recommend not using TemplateVariableInfo at all:
```
cc_binary(
  name = 'foo',
  srcs = ['foo.cc'],
)

sh_test(
  name = 'bar',
  srcs = ['bar.sh'],
  data = [':foo'],
  args = ['$(location :foo)'],
)
```

The test will have the relative path to foo passed in (in my test, it gets ./foo, since they are in the same directory). This saves all the deal with writing a custom rule and using TemplateVariableInfo, especially since in your use case you still need an actual dependency on foo, if you want it to be available as an input to your test.

review_comments: What's the significance of "unloaded" in this naming?
UnloadedToolchainContext is the class that the ToolchainResolver generates, and the load() method on UnloadedToolchainContext is what is being tested.

So the [docs](https://docs.bazel.build/versions/master/skylark/lib/platform_common.html#TemplateVariableInfo) describe this as:

> The provider used to retrieve the provider that contains the template variables defined by a particular toolchain

Can you parse this statement for me? We have to go through two providers to get the final info?

That is pretty ugly. Good thing I'm auditing the platform-related documentation this week.

TemplateVariableInfo contains a map of variable names to values, and can be used for automatic make variable expansion (ie, replacing ${FOO} in genrule's cmd, or various other places we handle make var expansion).
